blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en:
Conditional memory architectures such as DeepSeek Engram use input n n -grams to look up learned embeddings, expanding the capacity of large language models (LLMs) with limited additional computation.
Beyond model scaling, this architecture has demonstrated the potential to decouple factual knowledge storage from general-purpose computation, offering a promising route to updating factual knowledge while keeping the Transformer backbone fixed.
Realizing this potential is challenging because different expressions of a fact may activate different n n -gram embeddings, while updating shared embeddings can unintentionally change the model’s predictions about other facts.
We propose EngramEdit for decoupled knowledge updates through conditional memory. EngramEdit first computes target memory representations that make the model predict the updated fact across multiple expressions.
It then jointly updates the shared n n -gram embeddings to match these targets across expressions and edits, penalizing updates to frequently reused embeddings more strongly to preserve unrelated knowledge.
Experiments show that EngramEdit enables independent factual knowledge updates through conditional memory, achieving near-perfect editing success.
Revised knowledge is usable across unseen expressions and in multi-hop reasoning, with nearly 3 × \times the strongest baseline’s accuracy under chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting.
Unrelated knowledge and general capabilities are largely preserved even as factual updates accumulate.
These findings show that EngramEdit turns conditional memory into an editable knowledge interface, extending its role beyond model scaling to support decoupled knowledge updates.

除了模型规模外,这一架构还显示了将事实知识储存与普通用途计算脱钩的潜力,为更新事实知识提供了一条很有希望的路线,同时使变形器主干线固定下来。

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: Sparsity in large language models (LLMs) provides a promising way to scale model capacity without proportionally increasing per-token computation. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) [ 1 , 2 ] achieves this through conditional computation , activating only a subset of expert networks for each token. More recently, DeepSeek Engram [ 3 ] explores a complementary approach through conditional memory . At each token position, the model uses n n -grams of different lengths ending at that position to look up their learned embeddings. These embeddings provide input-dependent memory representations for the Transformer backbone computation (see Figure 1 (a)). This design is increasingly used to expand the capacity of LLMs such as DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash [ 4 ] and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next [ 5 ] .
blocks.zh: 大语言模型(LLMs)中的相容性为在不按比例地增加每克计算的情况下对模型容量进行分级提供了有希望的方法. Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) [1,2] 通过有条件的计算实现这一点,每个符号只激活一个子集的专家网络. 最近,DeepSeek Engram[3]通过有条件的内存探索一种互补方法. . 在每一个符号位置上,模型使用以该位置为终点的不同长度的n-克来查看其所学的嵌入. 这些嵌入为变形器主干线计算提供了依赖输入的内存表示(见图1(a))。 这种设计被越来越多地用于扩展DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash [4]和Quen3.8-Flash-Next [5]等LLMs的容量.

blocks.en: Beyond model scaling, conditional memory offers a promising architectural basis for decoupling factual knowledge storage from general-purpose computation in LLMs. In DeepSeek Engram, n n -gram embeddings store reusable local representations, while the Transformer backbone dynamically integrates and processes these representations in context [ 3 ] . Ablation experiments on Engram further show that disabling conditional memory severely degrades factual knowledge performance while largely preserving the ability to understand and reason about information provided in context (see Figure 1 (b)).
blocks.zh: 除了模型缩放外,有条件的内存为将事实知识存储与LLMs的通用计算脱钩提供了一个有希望的建筑基础. 在DeepSeek Engram中,n-gram嵌入存储可重用本地表示,而变形器主干在上下文[3]中动态地整合并处理这些表示. Engram上的阅读实验进一步表明,使有条件的记忆失效严重地降低了事实知识的性能,同时在很大程度上保留了了解和解释所提供信息的能力(见图1(b))。

blocks.en: This division of roles suggests a promising possibility: independently update factual knowledge in conditional memory without modifying the general-purpose backbone. Such updates would turn conditional memory into an editable knowledge interface, allowing LLMs to revise outdated facts while largely preserving general capabilities. Prior work mainly studies model scaling [ 3 , 6 ] , personalization [ 7 ] , and domain adaptation [ 8 ] , leaving this potential for decoupled knowledge updates largely unexplored.
blocks.zh: 这种角色划分表明一种很有希望的可能性:独立地在有条件的内存中更新事实知识而不修改通用骨干. 这种更新将使有条件的内存变成一个可编辑的知识界面,让LLMs修改已过时的事实,同时基本上保留一般能力. 之前的工作主要是研究模型缩放[3,6],个性化[7],以及域名适应[8],使得这种脱钩知识更新的潜力基本上没有得到探讨.

blocks.en: However, updating factual knowledge through conditional memory is non-trivial because memory lookup is determined by n n -grams rather than facts. 1) Efficacy. Different facts being edited may require conflicting changes to a shared n n -gram embedding, so an update that makes one edit succeed may cause another to fail. 2) Generalization. Rephrasing the same fact may activate different n n -grams whose embeddings were not updated, causing the edit to fail on the new expression. 3) Specificity. Embeddings associated with shorter or more frequently used n n -grams are also activated by many unrelated inputs, so updating them may change unrelated factual predictions.
blocks.zh: 然而,通过有条件的内存来更新事实知识是非三角性的,因为内存的外观是由n-gram而不是由事实决定的. (1) 效力。 正在编辑的不同事实可能需要对共享 n-gram 嵌入进行相冲突的更改,因此,使一个编辑成功的一个更新可能导致另一个编辑失败. 2)通论. 重写同样的事实可能会激活嵌入未更新的不同n-克,导致编辑在新表达式上失败. 3)具体性. 与更短或更常使用的n-克相接的嵌入也由许多不相干的投入激活,因此更新它们可能会改变不相干的事实预测.

blocks.en: To enable decoupled knowledge updates through conditional memory, we propose EngramEdit . The key idea is to first compute memory representations that make the LLM predict the updated facts, and then jointly translate these target representations into updates to the underlying shared n n -gram embeddings. As shown in Figure 1 (c), we first generate multiple expressions of each fact to broaden n n -gram coverage. For each edit, a shared learnable perturbation is temporarily added to the memory representations of its expressions. Optimizing only this perturbation by backpropagating the prediction loss for the new fact produces a target memory representation for each expression (see Sec. 3.1 ). We then map each target to the n n -gram embeddings used by its expression, identifying embeddings shared across expressions and edits (see Sec. 3.2 ). The embedding updates are solved jointly to match these targets, with each shared embedding receiving one update that accounts for all expressions and edits using it. To preserve unrelated knowledge, we include stronger penalties on large updates to frequently reused embeddings in this joint optimization (see Sec. 3.3 ).
blocks.zh: 为了通过有条件的内存实现脱钩的知识更新,我们提议EngramEdit . 关键的想法是首先计算出能使LLM预测更新后的事实的内存表示,然后共同将这些目标表示转化为对基础共享n-gram嵌入的更新. 如图1(c)所示,我们首先对每个事实产生多种表达方式,以扩大n-gm的覆盖范围。 每次编辑时,都会在其表达式的内存表达中临时添加一个可学习的可扰动. 仅通过背传新事实的预测损失来优化这种扰动,为每个表达式产生目标内存表示(见Sec. 3.1. 然后,我们将每个目标映射到其表达式所使用的n-gram嵌入,确定在表达式和编辑中共享的嵌入(见Sec. 3.2)。 嵌入式更新被联合解决,以匹配这些目标,每个共享嵌入式接收一个更新,该更新记录所有表达式并使用它进行编辑. 为了保存不相关的知识,我们对大规模更新进行更严厉的处罚,以便经常再利用嵌入这一联合优化(见3.3.)。

blocks.en: Our experiments show that EngramEdit enables effective and generalizable factual knowledge updates through conditional memory while largely preserving unrelated knowledge and general capabilities. 1) Factual knowledge can be effectively updated. By updating only conditional memory, EngramEdit achieves near-perfect editing success on both CounterFact [ 9 ] and ZsRE [ 10 ] . 2) Updated knowledge remains usable. EngramEdit achieves strong generalization to unseen expressions, and the revised facts support multi-hop reasoning. On MQuAKE [ 11 ] , it achieves nearly 3 × \times the strongest baseline’s multi-hop accuracy under chain-of-thought (CoT) prompting. 3) Unrelated knowledge and general capabilities are largely preserved. Overall performance on unrelated factual queries and general-ability tasks remains largely unchanged during extended sequential editing. Together, these findings show that EngramEdit turns conditional memory into an editable knowledge interface for decoupled knowledge updates. This extends its role beyond model scaling and opens a promising path toward LLMs that continually update their knowledge while largely preserving their general capabilities.
blocks.zh: 我们的实验表明,EngramEdit能够通过有条件的内存有效而通俗地更新事实知识,同时在很大程度上保留不相关的知识和一般能力. 1)事实知识可以有效更新. EngramEdit通过仅更新有条件的内存,在"反事实"[9]和"ZsRE"[10]上都实现了近乎完美的编辑成功. (2) 最新知识仍然可用。 图标 编辑实现强通化到隐形表达式,修改后的事实支持多跳推理. 在MQuake [11] 上,它实现了近3×\时最强基线的多跳精度,在思维链(COT)的提示下. (3) 无关联的知识和一般能力基本上得到保存。 在延长的相继编辑期间,不相关的事实查询和一般可操作性任务的总体表现基本保持不变。 这些发现一起表明EngramEdit将有条件的内存转化为一个可以编辑的知识界面,用于解开相通的知识更新. 这扩大了其作用,超越了模型规模,为不断更新其知识,同时在很大程度上保留其一般能力的法学硕士开辟了一条有希望的道路。

blocks.en: 3 Method
blocks.zh: 3 方法

blocks.en: In this section, we present EngramEdit for decoupled knowledge updates through conditional memory (see Figure 2 ). For each edit batch, we first compute target memory representations that make the LLM predict the updated facts across expressions (see Section 3.1 ). We then map each expression to its activated n n -grams, identifying those shared across expressions and edits (see Section 3.2 ). Finally, we jointly solve for a single update per embedding to match the targets using reuse-based regularization (see Section 3.3 ). Algorithm 1 in App. A.4 summarizes the complete procedure.
blocks.zh: 在本节中,我们提出EngramEdit,用于通过条件内存来解开相关知识更新(见图2). 对于每批编辑,我们首先计算出目标内存表示,使LLM可以预测跨表达式的最新事实(见第3.1节. 然后,我们将每个表达式映射到其已激活的n-克,确定在表达式和编辑中共享的表达式(见第3.2节)。 最后,我们共同解决每套嵌入一次更新的问题,以便通过基于再利用的正规化来配合目标(见第3.3节)。 App.A.4中的算法 1总结了完整的程序.

blocks.en: In this section, we conduct experiments to address the following research questions: • RQ1: How effectively does EngramEdit update factual knowledge through conditional memory while preserving unrelated knowledge? • RQ2: How well does EngramEdit preserve general capabilities during knowledge updates? • RQ3: How do EngramEdit’s design choices affect editing performance? • RQ4: How do EngramEdit’s memory updates support the LLM’s use of revised knowledge?

blocks.en: 4.1 Experimental Setup

blocks.en: On CounterFact [ 9 ] and ZsRE [ 10 ] , we report Efficacy (success on edited prompts), Generalization (success on held-out paraphrases not used during editing), Specificity (performance on unrelated queries), and their arithmetic mean, Utility. On CounterFact, we also report Fluency and Consistency for generated text. MQuAKE [ 11 ] measures multi-hop use of updated facts through answer accuracy. Following AlphaEdit [ 13 ] , we report mean task-level F1 across six general-ability tasks. See Apps. B.1 and B.2 for dataset examples and metric definitions.
blocks.zh: 关于"反事实"[9]和"ZsRE [10]",我们报告效果(在已编辑的提示上成功),"通论"(在编辑时没有使用的被搁置的参数上成功),"具体性"(在无关的询问上的表现),以及它们的算术平均值"效用". 关于反事实,我们还报告生成文本的流畅性和一致性。 MQuake [11] 测量通过答案精确度多跳使用更新的事实. 跟着阿尔法 编辑[13],我们报告是指6个通用可操作性任务的任务级别F1. 数据集示例和计量定义见Apps.B.1和B.2.

blocks.en: We compare editors applicable to MoE LLMs: FT, FT-L [ 15 ] , AdaLoRA [ 16 ] , UnKE [ 17 ] , and MoEEdit [ 14 ] . To compare direct memory fine-tuning, we include Memory-FT (Subject) and Memory-FT (All Tokens), which update n n -gram embeddings activated at the last subject token or all token positions in the original edit prompts, respectively. All experiments use LongCat-Flash-Lite [ 6 ] , with sequential batch editing. See Apps. B.3 and B.4 for details.
blocks.zh: 我们比较了适用于教育部法学硕士的编辑:FT、FT-L[15]、AdaLora[16]、UnKE[17]和MoEedit[14]。 为了比较直接的内存微调,我们包括了内存-FT(Subject)和内存-FT(All Tokens),它们分别更新了在上个主题符上激活的n-gram嵌入或原始编辑提示中的所有符号位置. 所有实验都使用"长卡-快克-快克"(LongCat-Flash-Lite [6]),并有相继的批次编辑. 详情见Apps.B.3和B.4。

blocks.en: To evaluate how effectively EngramEdit updates facts through conditional memory, we compare it with the baselines after 2,000 sequential edits on each of CounterFact and ZsRE (see Table 1 ). We further apply edits from 3,000 MQuAKE cases to test whether the updated facts support multi-hop reasoning (see Figure 3 ). We apply standard prompting for direct answers and CoT prompting for step-by-step reasoning before answering. We observe that:
blocks.zh: 为了评价EngramEdit如何有效地通过有条件的内存来更新事实,我们将它与Found Fact和ZsRE的每集2000个相继编辑后的基线进行比较(见表一. 我们进一步应用3000 MQuake 案例的编辑来测试更新的事实是否支持多跳推理(见图3). 我们采用标准,要求直接回答,COT在回答前要求逐步推理。 我们注意到:

blocks.en: • On CounterFact, EngramEdit achieves similar Efficacy to MoEEdit and MFT-S but much higher Generalization; on ZsRE, it leads in both metrics (see Table 1 ). Comparable success on edited prompts, therefore, does not imply comparable recall through other expressions. EngramEdit addresses this gap by updating embeddings across expressions, since different wordings can activate different n n -grams. Its advantages persist through 5,000 sequential edits, showing that revised facts remain accessible as further updates accumulate (see App. C.1.1 for details). • On MQuAKE, EngramEdit, and FT have similar accuracy under standard prompting. With CoT, EngramEdit achieves nearly 3 × \times the accuracy of the strongest baseline and leads across all hop groups, as shown in Figure 3 . This improvement shows that facts updated through conditional memory can be used in multi-hop reasoning. During CoT reasoning, intermediate steps can activate updated embeddings for the facts used, allowing revised information to guide subsequent steps. The advantage extends through four-hop cases, supporting the use of updated knowledge in longer reasoning chains (see App. C.1.2 for full results). • On ZsRE, EngramEdit’s Specificity remains close to the pre-edit level, whereas FT-L, AdaLoRA, UnKE, and MoEEdit exceed it. These higher scores do not by themselves establish better preservation, because Specificity counts newly correct answers as well as retained correct answers. The correctness transition analysis shows that corrections to previously wrong, unrelated predictions contribute to the baselines’ gains and that EngramEdit retains most initially correct predictions (see App. C.1.3 for further analysis). This provides additional evidence that its knowledge updates largely preserve performance on unrelated queries. • EngramEdit achieves the highest Utility on CounterFact and ZsRE, with Specificity close to pre-edit levels, and also leads in Fluency and Consistency. Together, these results show that EngramEdit supports effective and generalizable knowledge updates through conditional memory while largely preserving unrelated knowledge.

Both methods restrict editing to selected n n -gram embeddings, and EngramEdit further penalizes large changes to frequently reused embeddings to limit effects on unrelated tasks. blocks.en: 4.4 In-Depth Analysis
blocks.zh: 4.4 深度分析

blocks.en: To isolate each component’s contribution, we compare five variants on CounterFact and ZsRE, with other settings held fixed. w/o Joint solves embedding updates independently for each expression. w/o Freq. and w/o Len. remove the weighting that increases penalties for more frequent and shorter n n -grams, respectively. w/o Reg. removes reuse-based regularization, and w/o Reg. & Expr. additionally removes generated expressions. From Table 2 , we observe that: 1) Removing joint allocation substantially lowers Efficacy and Generalization on both datasets. This shows that jointly considering the targets of all expressions sharing an embedding helps the model recall revised facts across expressions. 2) Removing generated expressions from the unregularized variant substantially lowers Generalization. Generated expressions, therefore, mainly support cross-expression recall by covering the different n n -grams activated by alternative wordings. 3) Removing reuse-based regularization lowers Efficacy and Specificity, and removing either frequency or length weighting also reduces Utility. The regularization thus helps preserve unrelated knowledge by limiting changes to embeddings reused by other inputs. Our analysis further shows that over 92% of new errors on unrelated queries involve activation of updated embeddings (see App. C.3.2 ).

blocks.en: To distinguish the benefit of additional expressions from how they are used, we first compare MoEEdit, MFT-S, MFT-A, and EngramEdit with the same generated expressions per fact on CounterFact (see Figure 5 (a)). We then vary expression use in EngramEdit’s target computation and memory mapping, keeping other settings fixed (see Figure 5 (b)). All variants retain the original edit prompt. Coverage is the percentage of held-out paraphrases that activate an embedding updated for the same fact. We observe that: 1) With the same generated expressions, EngramEdit outperforms MFT-S in Generalization at similar Efficacy and Specificity. EngramEdit’s target computation and joint memory updating thus use these expressions more effectively for recall under different wordings (see App. C.2.1 for full results). 2) Using generated expressions for memory mapping increases Coverage and yields most of the Generalization gain, because the expanded set of updated n n -grams allows more held-out paraphrases to activate fact-related embeddings. An additional analysis of memory activation supports this explanation: the roughly 2% of held-out paraphrases activating no fact-related embeddings account for half of generalization failures (see App. C.3.2 ). With Coverage unchanged, also using these expressions for target computation further improves Generalization by optimizing targets across expressions.

EngramEdit 的目标计算和联合内存更新,因此在不同的用词下更有效地使用这些用词来召回(完整结果见App.C.2.1)。 2) 使用生成的表达式来进行内存映射可以增加覆盖度并产生大部分通化增益,因为被扩展的一组被更新的n-gram允许更多的被持有的参数来激活与事实相关的嵌入. 对内存活化的补充分析支持了这一解释:大约2%的被搁置解释激活了不与事实有关的嵌入,占通化失败的一半(见App.C.3.2.)。 在覆盖面不变的情况下,在目标计算时也使用这些表达式,通过优化各种表达式的目标,进一步提高了通用性.

blocks.en: To test whether the LLM uses the updated conditional memory to predict revised facts, we compare normal inference with disabling updates for the evaluated fact, randomly selecting other updates matched in number and n n -gram length, or all updates. All conditions use the same model after CounterFact editing and retain the original embeddings. As shown in Figure 5 (c), fact-related disabling sharply lowers Efficacy and Generalization, almost matching the effect of disabling all updates. In contrast, matched random disabling leaves Efficacy and Generalization unchanged. An additional analysis of prediction preferences shows that fact-related disabling makes the model favor original over revised facts on average (see App. C.3.1 ). These results show that the LLM relies on the fact-related memory updates to access and utilize revised knowledge.
blocks.zh: 为了测试LLM是否使用更新的有条件内存来预测被修改的事实,我们比较了正常推论和对被评价事实的无效更新,随机选择其他与数字和n-gram长度相匹配的更新,或者所有更新. 所有条件在"反事实"编辑后都使用同一种模式并保留了原始嵌入. 如图5(c)所示,与事实有关的功能障碍大大降低了效能和通俗化,几乎与所有更新功能障碍的效果相匹配。 相比之下,匹配的随机断裂叶效果和通缩不变. 对预测偏好所作的进一步分析表明,与事实有关的缺陷使得模型偏向于原始事实而不是平均订正事实(见App.C.3.1.)。 这些结果表明,LLM依赖于与事实相关的内存更新来访问和利用被修改的知识.

blocks.en: 5 Related Work
blocks.zh: 5 相关工作

blocks.en:
Lookup-based memory architectures expand model capacity through sparse access to stored vectors, as in Product-Key Memory [ 18 ] and Memory Layers at Scale [ 19 ] . A related line uses n n -gram embeddings to associate local token or byte sequences with reusable representations.
1) Model scaling. Byte Latent Transformer [ 20 ] , OverEncoding [ 21 ] , and SCONE [ 22 ] use n n -gram representations to enrich model inputs with local context at limited inference cost. Engram [ 3 ] and LongCat-Flash-Lite [ 6 ] further explore n n -gram-based memory to scale LLM capacity. For memory construction, Memory Grafting [ 23 ] builds frozen conditional memory offline from another model’s hidden states for pre-training. Related n n -gram-based designs are also used in Qwen3.8-Flash-Next [ 5 ] and DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash [ 4 ] .
2) Model adaptation. Conditional memory has also been adapted for personalization through user-specific embedding updates in User as Engram [ 7 ] and for domain adaptation in Engram Adapter [ 8 ] . Our work develops EngramEdit to use pretrained conditional memory as an editable knowledge interface, enabling decoupled factual updates while largely preserving unrelated knowledge and general capabilities.

基于搜索的内存架构通过对存储向量的少量访问来扩展模型容量,如Product-Key内存[18]和"规模的内存层"中. 相關行使用n-gram嵌入来将本地令牌或字节序列与可再用表示相配合.
1) 模型缩放. 字节Latent Transformer [20],OverEncoding [21],和SCONE [22] 使用n-gram表示法,以有限的推论成本来丰富本地上下文的模型输入. Engram [3] 和 LongCat-Flash-Lite [6] 进一步探索n-gram的内存来放大LLM容量. 对于内存构造,记忆取出[23]从另一个模型的隐藏状态下建立被冻结的有条件内存进行预训. 相关的n-gram设计也被用于Quen3.8-Flash-Next [5]和DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash [4].
2)模型改造. 有条件的内存也通过用户特有嵌入更新在用户中被改编为Engram [7],并被改编为Engram Adapter [8]中的域名适应. 我们的工作开发了EngramEdit,将预先训练过的有条件内存用作可编辑的知识界面,可以解开事实更新,同时基本上保留无关的知识和一般能力.

blocks.en:
KE methods can be grouped according to whether they modify the LLM’s original parameters.
1) Parameter-preserving methods. These methods supply updated knowledge through external information or additional components, keeping the original parameters fixed. SERAC [ 24 ] uses an edit cache, and IKE [ 25 ] uses in-context demonstrations. Larimar [ 26 ] , WISE [ 27 ] , and NeuralDB [ 28 ] use additional weights or memory components.
2) Parameter-modifying methods. More directly related to our work, these methods update existing model parameters. Constrained fine-tuning [ 15 ] limits parameter changes during optimization, while MEND [ 29 ] learns to transform editing gradients into weight updates. ROME [ 9 ] and MEMIT [ 12 ] use locate-then-edit to first compute target FFN outputs for new facts, then solve for the corresponding weight updates. UnKE [ 17 ] extends parameter-modifying editing to unstructured knowledge. To preserve unrelated knowledge during parameter updates, AlphaEdit [ 13 ] projects parameter changes into the null space of a preservation set. For different model architectures, STEM [ 30 ] revises facts through token-indexed embedding substitution, while MoEEdit [ 14 ] jointly updates MoE experts with constraints on routing shifts. EngramEdit focuses on realizing the potential of pretrained conditional memory for decoupled knowledge updates.

KE方法可以根据它们是否修改了LLM的原始参数来分组.
(1) 参数保存方法。 这些方法通过外部信息或其他组件提供更新的知识,使原始参数保持不变. SERAC [24] 使用编辑缓存,而IKE [25] 使用内文演示. Larimar [26],WISE [27],和神经数据库 [28] 使用额外的重量或内存组件.
2) 参数修改方法。 这些方法更直接地与我们的工作有关,更新了现有的模型参数。 限制微调[15]在优化期间限制参数变化,而MEND[29]则学习将编辑梯度转化为重量更新. ROME [9]和MEMIT [12] 使用定位-当时-编辑来先为新事实计算目标FFN输出,再为相应的重量更新解析. UnKE [17] 将参数修改编辑扩展至无结构化知识. 为了在参数更新过程中保存不相关的知识,AlphaEdit [13] 工程参数会改变为保存集的无效空间. 对于不同的模型架构,STEM [30]通过符号索引嵌入替换来修改事实,而MOEEEdit [14] 联合更新了教育部的专家,限制了路由转移. 图标 编辑专注于实现预受训练的有条件内存对脱钩知识更新的潜力.

blocks.en: 6 Conclusion and Future Work
blocks.zh: 6. 结论和今后的工作

blocks.en: In this work, we propose EngramEdit for decoupled knowledge updates via conditional memory, jointly updating shared n n -gram embeddings with reuse-based regularization. Experiments show high editing success and generalization, multi-hop use of updated facts, and largely preserved unrelated knowledge and general capabilities. These findings show that EngramEdit enables decoupled knowledge updates in LLMs through conditional memory, extending its role beyond model scaling to an editable knowledge interface. Future work can explore other conditional memory architectures and model scales, and efficient, stable updates to more facts at higher frequencies.
blocks.zh: 在这项工作中,我们提出EngramEdit,用于通过有条件的内存来解开相通的知识更新,联合更新共享n-gram嵌入,并基于再利用的正则化. 实验显示编辑成功和通俗化程度高,多跳使用更新的事实,并在很大程度上保留了无关的知识和通俗能力. 这些研究结果表明EngramEdit通过有条件的内存,可以解开LLMs中的知识更新,将其角色从模型缩放扩展到可编辑的知识界面. 未来的工作可以探索其他有条件的内存架构和模型尺度,并在更高的频率对更多事实进行高效而稳定的更新.

blocks.en: Ethics statement
blocks.zh: 道德操守说明

blocks.en: EngramEdit is intended to help LLMs keep factual knowledge up to date, but the ability to revise knowledge can also be misused to introduce false or misleading content. Our evaluation uses existing benchmarks, where counterfactual edit targets serve as experimental test cases and should not be treated as verified real-world facts. Responsible use therefore requires verifying factual updates, restricting editing access to authorized users, and auditing intended and unintended effects.

blocks.en: This section describes the datasets, evaluation, baselines, and implementation details for the experiments in Section 4 .

blocks.en: B.1 Datasets
blocks.zh: B.1 数据集

blocks.en: The editing benchmarks test factual recall and the use of revised facts in reasoning. A separate set of tasks measures general capabilities after editing.
blocks.zh: 编辑基准检验了事实召回和在推理中使用订正事实的情况。 一套单独的任务在编辑后衡量一般能力.

blocks.en: CounterFact [ 9 ] tests counterfactual changes to factual associations. We use the MultiCounterFact release provided with MEMIT for batched editing [ 12 ] . Each case contains an edit request e i e_{i} and its prompt (see Section 2 ), held-out paraphrases, neighborhood prompts about other subjects whose facts should remain unchanged, and generation prompts. Held-out paraphrases are used only for evaluation; generated expressions are used during editing. Table 3 illustrates an edit request and its evaluation prompts.
blocks.zh: 反事实[9]检验事实关联的反事实变化. 我们使用MEMIT提供的MultiCounterFact发布,进行分批编辑[12]. 每个案例都包含编辑请求 e i e_{i} 及其即时(见第2节), 被搁置的解说, Hold-out 参数仅用于评价;生成的表达式用于编辑. 表3显示了编辑请求及其评价提示。

blocks.en: ZsRE [ 10 ] represents factual associations as questions and answers. We use the editing evaluation split distributed with MEMIT [ 12 ] , taking the first reference answer as the editing target. Each case pairs the edit question with a held-out paraphrase and an unrelated question–answer pair from Natural Questions. The edit therefore requests the supplied factual answer, not a counterfactual replacement. An example question, its target answer, and the evaluation questions are shown in Table 3 .
blocks.zh: ZsRE [10]代表事实关联作为问答. 我们使用与MEMIT一起分发的编辑评价分拆[12],将第一个参考答案作为编辑目标. 每个案例都将编辑问题与一个搁置的解说和来自自然问题的一个不相干的问题解答组合起来。 因此,编辑要求提供事实答案,而不是反事实替代。 一个例子问题、目标答案和评价问题见表3。

blocks.en: MQuAKE [ 11 ] tests whether revised facts can be combined to answer multi-hop questions. We use 3,000 counterfactual cases covering two- to four-hop reasoning. Each case contains one or more fact-level edit requests, variants of a multi-hop question, and the answer implied by the revised facts, with accepted aliases. Table 3 shows how multiple fact edits change the answer to one multi-hop question.
blocks.zh: MQuake [11]测试修改后的事实是否可以合并以回答多跳问题. 我们用3000个反事实案件 包括两到四起推理 每个案例包含一个或多个事实级编辑请求,多跳题的变体,以及修改后的事实所隐含的答案,并有被接受的别名. 表3显示多个事实编辑如何将答案更改为一个多跳问题.

blocks.en: Following AlphaEdit [ 13 ] , we evaluate SST (SST-2) [ 31 ] for sentiment classification, MRPC [ 32 ] for paraphrase recognition, and CoLA [ 33 ] for linguistic acceptability. RTE [ 34 ] and NLI [ 35 ] test textual entailment, and MMLU [ 36 ] tests knowledge across multiple subjects. We use 100 examples per task; none are included in the edit requests.
blocks.zh: 跟着阿尔法 编辑 [13],我们评价 SST (SST-2) [31] 的情绪分类,MRPC [32] 的释义识别,CoLA [33] 的语言可接受性. RTE [34] 和 NLI [35] 测试文本内涵, MMLU [36] 测试多个学科的知识. 我们每次任务使用100个实例;编辑请求中没有包含任何实例.

Both use the benchmark’s demonstrations and greedy decoding, with maximum generation lengths of 32 and 128 tokens, respectively. We extract the first nonempty answer line for standard prompting, removing an optional answer label, and the final Answer: line for CoT. Predictions and reference answers are normalized for capitalization, whitespace, and boundary punctuation. A prediction is correct if it exactly matches the revised answer or an accepted alias. A case is correct if at least one of its question variants is answered correctly. We report the percentage of correct cases.

blocks.en: B.3 Baselines
blocks.zh: B.3 基线

blocks.en: We compare gradient-based expert editing, MoE-specific locate-then-edit, and direct conditional memory fine-tuning. AlphaEdit’s original update rule applies to a dense FFN projection [ 13 ] . We exclude it because applying that rule to routed experts requires an additional choice of experts and update allocation [ 14 ] . The gradient-based baselines use the model’s existing routed computation, with editable parameters specified below.
blocks.zh: 我们比较基于梯度的专家编辑,MOE特定定位时编辑,直接有条件的内存微调. AlphaEdit的原始更新规则适用于密集的FFN投影 [13]. 我们将其排除在外,因为对路由专家适用该规则需要另外选择专家和更新分配[14]。 基于梯度的基线使用该模型现有的路由计算,下文具体说明可编辑参数。

blocks.en: FT uses gradient descent to update selected model parameters so that edit prompts produce the desired answers. FT-L additionally bounds each parameter change to limit deviation from the model entering the edit batch [ 15 ] . In our MoE adaptation, both methods update expert FFN down-projections at layer 7. They use up to 25 epochs per edit batch, a learning rate of 5 × 10 − 4 5\times 10^{-4} , and optimization minibatches of one example. FT-L bounds each parameter change by 10 − 4 10^{-4} .
blocks.zh: FT使用梯度回落来更新所选模型参数,使编辑提示产生所期望的答案. FT-L附加了每个参数的修改以限制与输入编辑批次的模型的偏差[15]. 在我们的教育部适应中,两种方法都更新了专家FFN第7层的倒置投影. 每个编辑批次使用最多25个时段,5×10−4 5\times 10×4}的学习率,以及一个例子的优化小管. FT-L 将每个参数以 10 - 4 10 - 4 = 4 = 修改 。

blocks.en: AdaLoRA [ 16 ] learns low-rank updates to weight matrices while keeping the pretrained weights fixed. It allocates more of the rank budget to important update components and prunes less important ones. We apply it to expert down-projections at layer 7, optimizing the prediction loss on edit prompts with initial rank 12, target rank 8, and scaling parameter 32. It uses 25 epochs per edit batch, a learning rate of 5 × 10 − 4 5\times 10^{-4} , and optimization minibatches of one example.
blocks.zh: AdaLORA [16] 学习低等更新到重量矩阵,同时保持被预先训练的重量固定. 它将更多的分级预算分配给重要的更新部分,并花掉不太重要的部分。 我们把它应用于第7层的专家倒计时,优化编辑提示的预测损失,初始排行12,目标排行8,并缩放参数32. 每个编辑批次使用25个纪元,学习率为5×10−4 5\times 10×4},并优化一个例子的小型管子.

blocks.en: UnKE [ 17 ] edits knowledge by first computing target Transformer-block representations that lead to the desired answers. It then updates block parameters to match these targets while retaining the outputs on preservation examples. In our MoE adaptation, we fit the layer-7 block outputs by updating the experts’ gate, up-, and down-projections; attention and router parameters remain fixed. Target computation uses up to 25 steps at learning rate 0.5 0.5 , and parameter fitting uses up to 50 steps at learning rate 2 × 10 − 4 2\times 10^{-4} .
blocks.zh: UnKE [17] 通过第一个计算目标变形器-块表示来编辑知识,从而得到所期望的答案. 然后更新块参数,与这些目标相匹配,同时保留保存实例的产出. 在我们对教育部的适应中,我们通过更新专家的上下预测门来适应第7层的输出;注意力和路由参数仍然固定。 目标计算使用最高为25步的学习速率0.5分,参数配位使用最高为50步的学习速率2×10−4 2.\times 10^{-4}.

blocks.en: MoEEdit [ 14 ] jointly updates expert FFN down-projections so that their router-weighted outputs match the editing targets. To preserve outputs on unrelated inputs and limit downstream routing shifts, it constrains each expert’s update using a null-space projection built from preservation inputs. The updates are solved one expert at a time through block coordinate descent. We edit layer 7, using up to 25 target-computation steps at learning rate 0.1 0.1 and four block coordinate descent passes. The per-expert null-space projections use statistics from 100,000 Wikipedia samples.
blocks.zh: MoEEedit [14] 联合更新了专家FFN下投影,使其路由器加权输出与编辑目标相匹配. 为了保留无关投入的产出并限制下游的出行方向变化,它利用从保存投入中构建的空地投影来限制每位专家的更新。 更新通过块坐标下降一次解决一名专家. 我们编辑第7层,使用最多25个目标计算步骤,学习速度为0.1 0.1和4个区块坐标下传. 每个专家的空地预测使用10万个维基百科样本中的统计数据.

blocks.en: This baseline directly fine-tunes conditional memory to predict the desired answers, restricting updates to embeddings activated at the last subject-token position of each original edit prompt. Since this selects a limited set of n n -grams, we store one cumulative update vector per exact n n -gram, as in EngramEdit. We optimize these vectors by backpropagating the prediction loss and add them whenever their n n -grams are activated, including outside subject positions. The pretrained hashed tables, token embeddings, memory projection layers, and backbone remain fixed.
blocks.zh: 此基准直接微调条件内存,以预测想要的答案,将更新限制在每一个原始编辑提示的最后一个主题键位置所激活的嵌入. 由于此选项选择了有限的 n- grams 一组, 我们保存了每个精确 n- gram 的一个累积更新矢量, 如 EngramEdit 中 。 我们通过反向宣传预测损失来优化这些向量,并在它们n-克激活时加入,包括外部对象位置. 被预先训练的散列表,活字嵌入,内存投影层,骨干都保持固定.

blocks.en: This variant expands direct memory fine-tuning to embeddings activated at every token position in the original edit prompts, using the same prediction loss. Storing a separate update vector for each n n -gram in this larger set would increase memory requirements. We therefore directly fine-tune the pretrained hashed tables, allowing rows activated at any token position to receive gradient updates while keeping all other parameters fixed. Both Memory-FT variants use n n -gram lengths 2, 3, and 4, up to 25 epochs per edit batch, a learning rate of 3 × 10 − 3 3\times 10^{-3} , and optimization minibatches of one example.

blocks.en: B.4 Implementation Details

blocks.en: We describe the shared model and editing setup, followed by EngramEdit’s target computation, memory mapping, and memory updating settings.
blocks.zh: 我们描述共享模型和编辑设置,然后是EngramEdit的目标计算、内存映射和内存更新设置。

blocks.en: B.4.1 Model and Editing Setup
blocks.zh: B.4.1 模式和编辑设置

blocks.en: All experiments use LongCat-Flash-Lite, a 68.5B-parameter MoE model with 31.4B parameters in n n -gram embeddings [ 6 ] , and run on two NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPUs. Its conditional memory uses suffix n n -grams of lengths 2, 3, and 4, with four hashed sub-tables per length. Each sub-table returns a 256-dimensional vector, which is linearly projected to the 3,072-dimensional token embedding space. At each position, the model averages the twelve projected vectors and the original token embedding before passing the result to the backbone. EngramEdit keeps the token embeddings and these projection matrices fixed.
blocks.zh: 所有实验都使用长Cat-Flash-Lite,一种68.5B参数的MOE模型,以n-gram嵌入为31.4B参数 [6],运行在两个NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 GPU上. 其有条件的内存使用后缀n-克长度为2、3和4的后缀n-克,每长有四个散列子表. 每个子表返回一个256维向量,线性地投射到3,072-维符号嵌入空间. 在每一个位置,模型平均十二个预测向量和原始的活性符号嵌入后再将结果传递给主干. 图标 编辑时保持符号嵌入和这些投影矩阵的固定.

blocks.en: An edit batch contains the requests applied together; an optimization minibatch contains the examples used in one gradient step. The main CounterFact and ZsRE experiments apply 2,000 edits in batches of 100, with each batch starting from the model state produced by preceding batches. The longer runs extend editing to 5,000 facts. For MQuAKE, we shuffle the 3,000 cases once with seed 0 and use the same case IDs and hop labels for all methods. Each batch contains 100 cases, with all their fact-level edit requests applied together, so a batch can contain more than 100 fact edits.
blocks.zh: 编辑批次包含一起应用的请求;优化小批次包含一个梯度步骤中使用的例子. 主要的CounterFact和ZsRE实验应用了2000个分批100的编辑,每批从前一批生产的模型状态开始. 更长的时间将编辑范围扩大到5,000个事实。 对MQuake来说,我们用0号种子洗刷了3000个病例,并且对所有方法都使用相同的病例ID和hop标签. 每批包含100个案例,它们所有的事实级编辑请求一起应用,因此一批可以包含超过100个的事实编辑.

blocks.en: CounterFact trajectories are evaluated every 100 edits, and ZsRE trajectories are compared at common intervals of 200 edits. General capabilities are evaluated before editing and every 500 edits through 5,000 sequential CounterFact edits, using 100 examples per task (see Appendix B.1 ).
blocks.zh: 反事实轨迹每100个编辑得到评价,而ZsRE轨迹则以200个编辑的共同间隔进行比较. 在编辑前对一般能力进行评估,每500次编辑通过5000个相继的"反事实"编辑,每个任务使用100个实例(见附录B.1.

blocks.en: B.4.2 Target Computation and Memory Mapping
blocks.zh: B.4.2 目标计算和记忆映射

blocks.en: For each edit request, we ask the model to generate four semantically equivalent expressions before editing, using the prompt and filtering rules in Appendix A.2.1 . The retained expressions and original edit prompt form the expression set used for target computation and memory mapping.
blocks.zh: 对于每个编辑请求,我们请模型在编辑前使用附录A.2.1中的即时和过滤规则生成四个等同的表达式. 保留表达式和原始编辑即时构成用于目标计算和内存映射的表达式集.

blocks.en: During target computation, we evaluate each expression both alone and after each of five model-generated prefix contexts, which vary the surrounding text without rephrasing the edit request. The shared perturbation is added to the conditional memory representation before the first decoder block, while all decoder parameters remain fixed. Following the target readout in MEMIT [ 12 ] , we compute the NLL from the last decoder block’s hidden states using the model’s fixed final normalization and language-model head. This yields the final predictive distribution in Eq. 20 ; the KL preservation term also uses final-output probabilities.
blocks.zh: 在目标计算过程中,我们单独和在五个模型生成的前缀上下文的每个后评价每个表达式,这些上下文在不重写编辑请求的情况下会改变周围的文字. 在第一个解码器块之前,共享扰动被添加到有条件的内存表示中,而所有解码器参数仍然固定. 在MEMIT[12]的目标读出之后,我们用模型的固定最终正常化和语言模型头来计算最后一个解码器隐藏状态的NLL。 这得出Eq.20的最终预测分布;KL保存术语也使用最终输出概率.

Optimization stops when the total target-computation loss falls below 0.05 0.05 , checked every two steps.

blocks.en: We use expressions without prefix contexts for memory mapping. At each expression’s last subject-token position, we extract suffix n n -grams of lengths 2, 3, and 4, skipping incomplete windows and windows crossing an end-of-sequence token.
blocks.zh: 我们使用没有前缀上下文的表达式进行内存映射. 在每一个表达式的最后一个主题键位置上,我们提取后缀n-克的长度为2、3和4,跳过不完全的窗口和窗口通过一个序列结束符.

blocks.en: B.4.3 Memory Updating
blocks.zh: B.4.3 记忆更新

blocks.en: Conditional memory uses hashed tables to control the storage cost of a large n n -gram space. Editing only requires storing updates for the selected n n -grams. We therefore maintain a separate cumulative update vector for each edited n n -gram, indexed by its exact token sequence. Additional storage scales with the number of distinct edited n n -grams, and the exact indexing prevents hash collisions from coupling their updates. Each vector is added to the embedding output whenever its n n -gram is activated, while the pretrained tables remain fixed.
blocks.zh: 有条件的内存使用散列表来控制一个大 n-克空间的存储成本. 编辑只需要存储所选 n -克的更新 。 因此,我们为每个已编辑的n-克保持一个单独的累积更新矢量,按其确切的符号序列索引。 附加的存储缩放,带有不同的已编辑 n-克数,精确的索引可以防止散列相撞使其更新相接. 每个矢量在 n-克被激活时被添加到嵌入输出中,同时预加训练的表格仍然固定.

blocks.en: • EngramEdit preserves pre-edit F1 on SST and CoLA throughout editing, while RTE, MMLU, and NLI stay within four F1 points of their pre-edit scores. blocks.en: To examine how editing choices affect knowledge updating and preservation, we first compare editors with and without generated expressions. blocks.en: • Adding four generated expressions improves Generalization for MFT-S, MFT-A, and EngramEdit on both datasets, whereas MoEEdit’s Efficacy and Generalization decrease. blocks.en: To identify which n n -gram lengths support both effective updates and preservation, we compare eight editable-length configurations on CounterFact using 2,000 sequential edits in batches of 100. We test lengths 2, 3, and 4 individually, in pairs, and together, as well as the full combination with single-token ( n = 1 n=1 ) embedding updates. All settings use four generated expressions and reuse-based regularization; only the lengths eligible for embedding updates change. From Figure 9 , we observe that:

blocks.en: Figure 9 : Editable n n -gram lengths on CounterFact. The frame marks the default lengths 2, 3, and 4; n = 1 n=1 denotes single-token embedding updates. Small ± \pm values give CI half-widths.
blocks.zh: 图9:在"反事实"上可编辑n-克长度. 框架标记了默认长度为2、3和4;n = 1 n = 1 表示单托嵌入更新. 小 ±\pm 值给出 CI 半宽 。

blocks.en: • Among single-length settings, 2-grams achieve the highest Efficacy and Generalization, while longer n n -grams give higher Specificity. Shorter n n -grams therefore favor access across expressions, whereas longer ones favor preservation. This is because shorter token sequences can activate the same updated embedding across both paraphrases and unrelated inputs. • Combining lengths 2, 3, and 4 achieves the highest Efficacy, Generalization, and Utility, with higher Specificity than using 2-grams alone. This suggests that different lengths can complement each other. Shorter n n -grams support access across expressions, while longer ones provide more context-specific embeddings that can carry part of the update, reducing reliance on embeddings shared with unrelated inputs. • Excluding single-token embedding updates yields markedly higher Specificity than editing lengths 1–4, with no loss in Efficacy or Generalization. blocks.en: • All tested nonzero reuse coefficients yield higher Efficacy, Specificity, and Utility than disabling the reuse-based term, with little variation among them. The gains therefore do not depend on one precisely tuned strength. Changing the coefficient scales the reuse-based penalties but retains stronger constraints on frequently reused embeddings, which can help preserve unrelated knowledge across these settings. • All four metrics remain close across ridge coefficients, including zero. This shows that strong performance does not require a precisely tuned uniform penalty. Strong editing performance thus holds across the tested norm bounds. blocks.en: C.3 Analysis of Memory Use

blocks.en: To understand how revised facts are accessed through conditional memory, we first test whether successful recall depends on fact-related updates by selectively disabling them, extending Section 4.4 . With all updates enabled, we next group inputs by the updated embeddings they activate, then analyze how cross-edit sharing relates to editing outcomes as updates accumulate. These later analyses leave the edited model unchanged and identify associations, while disabling directly tests the effect of removing updates.
blocks.zh: 为了了解修改后的事实是如何通过有条件的内存获取的,我们首先测试成功召回是否取决于与事实相关的更新,有选择地使其失效,从而扩展了第4.4节. 随着所有更新的启用,我们将通过它们激活的更新嵌入来进行下一组输入,然后随着更新的积累,分析交叉编辑共享与编辑结果的关系. 这些后期分析使被编辑的模型保持不变并识别了关联,同时可以直接测试去除更新的效果.

blocks.en: To relate memory activation to generalization and preservation, we evaluate 4,000 held-out paraphrases and 20,000 neighborhood prompts after completing 2,000 sequential CounterFact edits, with all updates enabled. We observe that: • Among the 17,534 initially successful prompts, 96.77% remain successful and 3.23% regress; the regression rate in None is only 0.28%. Most previously correct predictions are thus retained, with especially strong preservation in None because these inputs do not directly use embedding updates. The 44 regressions in None may reflect finite-precision differences that reverse close answer rankings across inference runs. • Other only accounts for 79.72% of all regressions, whereas Current only accounts for 6.35% despite its higher within-group regression rate. Overall, 92.24% of regressions accompany activation of updated embeddings. Regressions are thus concentrated in inputs that activate updates for other edits. Different facts can share n n -grams, so an update for one fact can also affect unrelated predictions. This supports using reuse-based regularization to penalize large updates to frequently reused embeddings.

blocks.en: C.3.3 Cross-Edit Sharing
blocks.zh: C.3.3 跨编辑共享

blocks.en: To examine how cross-edit sharing relates to editing outcomes, we analyze the 5,000-edit CounterFact run every 100 edits. We track n n -grams selected at the last subject token of each fact’s original and four generated expressions. A fact belongs to Sharing if any selected n n -gram is also selected for another fact, and to No sharing otherwise. Figure 12 reports sharing rates and groups the saved final results. We observe that: • Sharing increases overall but involves only 285 of 22,778 updated n n -grams (1.25%) and 433 facts (8.66%) at 5,000 edits. Most embeddings are therefore selected for one fact; the higher fact-level rate reflects that a shared embedding serves multiple facts. • No sharing covers 91.34% of facts with 99.98% Efficacy and 96.7% Generalization, showing sustained editing success across expressions for most facts. Their selected embeddings are not shared with other edits, so different facts do not compete for updates to the same parameters. • Sharing contains 48 of the 49 Efficacy failures (97.96%), with lower Generalization but similar Specificity. Failures are thus concentrated in a small group of facts sharing updated embeddings, where different targets may require conflicting changes to the same parameters.
